description: PRE-EXISTING at HEAD (flakes ~50% on clean HEAD, independent of fz-f98.14.10.4 — transport PLAN is now stable, lib joined-callable test 20/20). matrix opaque_fn_value_join::build/run flakes on a native JIT/AOT boundary-return-lane mismatch: 'callable boundary return lanes must match: boundary=[ValueRef], body=[RawInt]'. DISTINCT subsystem from the transport shape-graph (14.10.4) — this is non-monotone boundary-return-lane derivation in native lowering (the callable-boxing-seam family, [[project_fz_callable_boxing_seam]]). A sorted_boundaries determinism attempt did not fully fix it and destabilized the input-anchor path (reverted). Likely the same earned-vs-fallback / schedule-independence discipline as 14.10.4 but in the return-lane path. Its own ticket; does not block 14.10.

comments.text: COORDINATOR SIGNAL 2026-07-10 on integration 9b4bca389: enum_take_drop_split native run still fails in this native callable ABI family. `cargo test --test fz2_cli native_enum_take_drop_split_preserves_tuple_accumulator_lists -- --nocapture` fails with artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan: native callable materialization for CallableId(20) has resolutions with incompatible physical ABI: executable 170 arg_reprs=[ValueRef, ValueRef], return_reprs=[RawAtom, ValueRef, RawAtom], return_tuple_arity=Some(2) vs executable 171 arg_reprs=[RawInt, ValueRef], return_reprs=[RawAtom, ValueRef], return_tuple_arity=Some(2). This is now a concrete blocker for closing fz-f98.14 after the original convergence/lowering fatal was retired.

UPGRADED FROM FLAKE TO DETERMINISTIC, with mechanism. The fz-6gb branch (fz-6gb/brand-blind-library-keying, uncommitted) makes this fire reliably: merging the run/1 transporter routes a 2-target FnRef union (each_a|each_b) through Enum.each's bridge into each_step's INDIRECT closure call, and the process SIGABRTs.

MECHANISM, traced end to end on opaque_fn_each_absent_return under fz2 run:
- each_step's mapper call lowers indirect: Term::CallClosure { closure, args, continuation } (native.rs ~1520, the non-direct arm of BackendTail::ClosureCall).
- The CONTINUATION's parameter reprs come from the CALLER-side return_flow source layout (return_lane_continuation_for_source_payload) -- the artifact plane, which settled a 1-lane return.
- The callee resolves through the BOUNDARY plane, whose return_form for the each mappers is ABSENT (the very thing the pinned test asserts): the wrapper invokes the continuation with ZERO return lanes.
- The arity mismatch scrambles the continuation's register ABI: the env slot receives an unwritten lane containing an f64 NaN (word 0xfffff0007fc00000), and the continuation's capture read aborts in fz_closure_get_capture_atom (index=1, first capture-atom read of the whole run).

So the two planes disagree about one fact -- how many lanes an indirect callable call returns -- and each was compiled against its own answer. Single-authority fix direction: the indirect closure-call's continuation must consume the BOUNDARY's return_form (or the two planes must be reconciled upstream in transport, which owns return layouts). The direct-call path already handles absent returns correctly, which is why the bug only fires when a union defers resolution to an indirect call.

REPRODUCER (deterministic, ~seconds): on the fz-6gb branch, fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_each_absent_return.fz. Bisection lever if needed: erasure of fn 33 (run/1) alone triggers it.

Related reds with the same signature family on that branch: enum_reduce_suspend x3, enum_take_drop_split x3, range_reduce3 halt/suspend lib pair -- the suspend/halt flavors of the same return-plane conflation.

fz-6gb is blocked on this; it is the last layer between the measured 4x compile win and green suites.

FIXED at dcb261133 (PR #94, stacked on #93). The return-lane conflation is closed; the SIGABRT is gone and opaque_fn_each_absent_return runs 1 2 3 on all three lanes.

ROOT, confirmed exactly as the mechanism comment predicted: the payload was reading the wrong fact. TransportPosition::ReturnPayload derived its layout from the CALLER's own return type and demand (world.activation_return + runtime.return_demand). But a callsite's return payload is the CALLSITE RESULT's contract. Those alias whenever the call is TAIL-positioned -- the result IS the caller's return -- which is why this survived so long and read as a schedule-dependent flake. For a DELIVERED result the two are different facts, and each_step's discarded fun.(entry) is the case that separates them: the caller returns a demanded acc (one ValueRef lane) while the discarded result carries no demand at all (zero lanes, the same zero the callee-side boundary derives as return_form: Absent).

FIX: a `callsite_result` helper names the tail's result value and whether it sits in tail position; the payload derives type+demand from that value in the delivered case and keeps the caller's return in the tail case. One fact, both halves of the calling convention. No change to the boundary plane, the direct-call path, demand, or keying.

The single-authority direction recorded earlier was right but pointed one step downstream (make the continuation consume the boundary's return_form). Fixing the payload derivation instead means the two planes never disagree in the first place, so nothing needs reconciling at the consumer.

ELIXIR CHECK: on the BEAM every call returns a value; there is no "absent". fz's zero-lane return is purely an optimization, and an optimization on a shared seam must be one fact both sides read.

TEST: compiler2_discarded_indirect_call_result_publishes_no_return_lanes pins it on each_step's callsite directly (asserted [ValueRef] before, empty after).

RESULTS: matrix 402/410 -> 407/410 (enum_reduce_suspend x3 and opaque_fn_each_absent_return run+build now green); lib opaque_callable_each + the range_reduce3 halt/suspend pair green; clippy --workspace 0 warnings; fmt clean.

NOT CLOSING YET: the 2026-07-10 coordinator signal on this ticket (native callable materialization for CallableId(20): members with incompatible physical ABI, return_reprs=[RawAtom, ValueRef, RawAtom] vs [RawAtom, ValueRef]) is the MIXED-MEMBER case, a different half of this ticket's surface. enum_take_drop_split is still red but now fails on a DIFFERENT guard (see the fz-6gb comment) -- re-verify whether the mixed-ABI signal still reproduces at this commit before doing more work here; it may already be gone.

VERIFIED AT main 417c5b0b5 (landed via PR #94, squash-merged as 375087922).

Both fixtures in this ticket's signature family are green on all three lanes:

    matrix::opaque_fn_value_join::{run,interp,build}          ... ok
    matrix::opaque_fn_each_absent_return::{run,interp,build}  ... ok

The reported mismatch ("callable boundary return lanes must match:
boundary=[ValueRef], body=[RawInt]") and the SIGABRT the 2026-08-24 comment
traced are both gone. The fix landed the single-authority direction that comment
predicted: a callsite's return payload derives from the CALLSITE RESULT's
contract, which aliases the caller's return only in tail position.

Its dependent fz-6gb is also verified and closed. Closing.

title: Native callable boundary return-lane mismatch flake (opaque_fn_value_join: boundary=[ValueRef] vs body=[RawInt])
